recent_posts.title: March 2026 Project Director Update
recent_posts.summary: The Rust Foundation board meeting from March 10, 2026 covered several key developments: a proposal for an AI-focused research initiative within the Foundation, the Symposium project joining the Rust Innovation Lab, early discussions on making crates.io more sustainable, ideas for a Rust Ecosystem Fund to help companies support important crates, Canonical joining as a Gold member, the Foundation joining DataDog's Open Source Program, ongoing work to address typosquatting attacks on crates.io, and progress on the C++ interoperability initiative.

recent_posts.title: crates.io: Help test our new web frontend
recent_posts.summary: The crates.io team has ported its frontend from Ember.js to Svelte 5 and is inviting public testing at https://crates.io/svelte/. The new Svelte app is designed as a 1:1 port, sharing session state and data with the existing Ember.js app. UI and visual regression tests already pass for both. If testing goes smoothly, Svelte will become the default frontend within weeks. Feedback can be submitted via GitHub or Zulip.

recent_posts.title: Infrastructure Team 2026 Q1 Recap and Q2 Plan
recent_posts.summary: The Rust Infrastructure Team's Q1 2026 recap covers migration to GitHub Rulesets, CI security improvements (Renovate bot, zizmor static analysis, crates-io-auth-action update), provisioning of new dev desktops with IPv6 support, upgrading the docs.rs instance with doubled RAM and CPU, SAML SSO with Google Workspace, and multiple Triagebot enhancements including a GitHub issue comments viewer, org-wide default configuration, user-info command, per-team rotation mode, and new Zulip commands for backports and issue priority. Q2 plans include finishing unfinished Q1 goals, further CI security and developer experience improvements, and distributing YubiKeys to teams with critical infrastructure access at Rust All Hands in May.

recent_posts.title: Program management update — March 2026
recent_posts.summary: The Rust program management team shares their March 2026 update covering team meeting restructuring, the 2026 Project Goals RFC, FLS release notes process improvements, a verifiable mirroring prototype for crates.io, the Rust Foundation Maintainers Fund RFC proposing a 'Maintainer in Residence' role, Outreachy internship participation, Rust for Linux const generics priorities, and Rust for CPython progress including Drop-with-context discussions and sanitizer compatibility. Notable releases include Rust 1.94.0/1.94.1, rustup 1.29.0, and a Cargo security advisory.

recent_posts.title: Leadership Council update — March 2026
recent_posts.summary: The Rust Leadership Council shares its March 2026 update covering new council members (Rémy Rakic as compiler team rep and Josh Triplett as libs team rep), a new Program Manager (Nurzhan Saken), and budget allocations from a $412k project priorities fund. Key spending includes $160k for the PM program, $100k for travel grants, $55k for a compiler-ops contract, and $25k for Outreachy mentorship. Ongoing work includes an RFC for the Rust Foundation Maintainers Fund and a significant policy discussion around AI-generated 'slop' contributions to the rust-lang/rust repository.

recent_posts.title: Program management update — February 2026
recent_posts.summary: The February 2026 Rust program management update introduces Nurzhan Saken as the new co-program manager alongside Tomas Sedovic. Key highlights include progress on the 2026 project goals cycle (targeting an RFC in March and a new goal period starting April), new program management infrastructure (a GitHub board and program-team repo), active C++/Rust interoperability problem-space mapping by a new contractor, and a signing & mirroring MVP proposal for Rustup targets. The update covers Rust for Linux's upcoming MSRV considerations tied to Debian 14 Forky, with notable features like arbitrary self types, field projections, immovable types, and relaxed orphan rules on the roadmap. A session with Miguel Ojeda shared lessons from Rust for Linux that are now informing the Rust for CPython effort. The Style team is seeking contributors, and Rust 1.94.0 and the 2025 State of Rust Survey results were published.

recent_posts.title: January & February 2026 Project Director Update
recent_posts.summary: The Rust Project Directors share a combined update from the Rust Foundation's January and February 2026 board meetings. Key highlights include: a new infrastructure engineer hired via Sovereign Tech Agency funding, crates.io frontend migration from EmberJS to Svelte, launch of a vulnerability surfacing security tab on crates.io, development of cargo-capslock for capability analysis, progress on Rust/C++ interoperability initiatives, AWS credit donation to the project, Rust Innovation Lab eligibility discussions, and upcoming RustConf announcements. The Foundation also held interviews with team leads to assess project health and needs.

recent_posts.title: This Development-cycle in Cargo: 1.94
recent_posts.summary: A development cycle summary covering Cargo changes merged during the Rust 1.94 window. Key updates include: target directory locking (merged with deferred items tracked), structured logging progress with new `cargo report rebuild` and `cargo report sessions` subcommands, TOML 1.1 support (newlines in inline tables), the experimental `cargo-cargofmt` tool for formatting Cargo.toml files, and `resolver.lockfile-path` config field replacing the `--lockfile-path` CLI flag. Design discussions cover workspace and configuration discovery edge cases, including a proposed `package.workspace = <bool>` opt-out mechanism. The plugin spotlight is `cargo-edit`, which provides `cargo upgrade` and `cargo set-version`.

recent_posts.title: Leadership Council March 2026 Representative Selections
recent_posts.summary: The Rust Leadership Council is beginning its March 2026 representative selection process. Half of the council terms end every six months, and affected teams must confirm their representative choices by March 20, 2026. Representatives can be any member from top-level teams or subteams, with a limit of two people from the same company on the council. Teams are encouraged to rotate representatives after three terms to prevent burnout and spread experience.

recent_posts.title: Program management update — January 2026
recent_posts.summary: Rust's program management team shares January 2026 updates: 60 project goals proposed for 2026 with new roadmap structure and application areas to attract industry funding. A second Program Manager (Nurzhan Saken) has been hired. Rust for Linux work continues with new language features like field projections and in-place initialization. Weekly meetings with CPython team explore bringing Rust into the Python interpreter. Cargo script feature nears stabilization, enabling single-file Rust programs with dependencies. Crates.io mirroring and verification work progresses with improved communication structure.
